source: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, Baseline Cyber Security Controls for Small and Medium Organizations, V1.2 (February 2020)

requirements.summary: Have a basic plan for responding to incidents of varying severity
Written plan naming who handles incidents and external contacts, with an up-to-date hard copy
Consider cyber insurance covering response and recovery, or document why not
Enable automatic patching for all software and hardware
Assess replacing anything that cannot update automatically, or patch it manually
Enable anti-malware that updates and scans automatically
Turn on built-in software firewalls on devices
Secure configurations: change default passwords, turn off unnecessary features, enable security features
Two-factor authentication wherever possible, and required for financial, admin, cloud admin, privileged, and executive accounts
Only force password changes on suspicion or evidence of compromise
Clear policies on password length, reuse, password managers, and writing passwords down
Invest in cyber security awareness and training for employees
Back up essential systems, make sure restores work, and consider offline off-site backups
Encrypt backups, restrict access to them, and keep long-term backups offline
Choose and document a mobile device ownership model
Separate work and personal data on mobile devices
Only install apps from trusted sources
Store sensitive information on mobile devices in an encrypted state
Consider an enterprise mobility management solution
Avoid open or unknown Wi-Fi and limit Bluetooth and NFC for sensitive data
Consider a VPN when using public Wi-Fi
Dedicated firewall at the internet boundary; isolate internet-facing servers
DNS firewall for outbound DNS requests
Secure connectivity, with VPN and two-factor for all remote access
Only secure Wi-Fi, preferably WPA2-Enterprise
Never connect public Wi-Fi networks to the corporate network
Isolate point-of-sale systems with a firewall
Implement DMARC on all email services
Email filtering at points of ingress and egress
Require SOC 3 reports from cloud service providers
Evaluate how outsourced IT providers handle and access your sensitive information
Evaluate the legal jurisdictions where providers store or use your data
Communicate securely with all cloud services
Two-factor on cloud admin accounts, separate from internal admin accounts
Websites address the OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities
Know the ASVS level each website needs to meet
Give accounts only what they need, and restrict admin privileges to an as-required basis
Use admin accounts only for admin tasks, not email or web browsing
Remove accounts and access when employees no longer need them
Consider centralized authorization control
Only organization-owned, encrypted portable media under asset control
Sanitize or destroy portable media before disposal
